title: An Urgent Response Is Needed to Artificial Intelligence in Schools and Colleges
author: Filling the Pail
summary: AI has made take-home assignments educationally meaningless: a teacher can ask AI to design an assignment, a student can ask AI to complete it, and a teacher can use AI to grade it, producing a perfect loop of automated non-education. Schools that continue assigning graded take-home work as if it is meaningful are accelerating the devaluation of credentials. The historical critique that examinations are artificial misses the point: their artificiality is precisely their strength, because they require students to produce something from their own minds rather than their own resources. The author argues for a passionate embrace and expansion of examinations as the only remaining reliable method of assessing what knowledge a person actually possesses. Examinations reflect what education should be -- an extraordinary space for developing the mind -- not a simulation of the soulless knowledge-lookup that characterizes most workplace activity. The urgency of the response is framed in terms of institutional survival: universities that fail to act risk bankruptcy.
points: * It is now possible for a teacher to assign with AI, a student to complete with AI, and a teacher to grade with AI -- rendering the entire take-home assignment cycle educationally void. * AI detection software is unreliable enough that accusing students of cheating on AI-generated work risks serious miscarriages of justice and endless appeals. * The artificial nature of examinations -- timed, isolated, technology-free -- is not a weakness but the source of their value: they assess what is inside a person's head. * Education should be about the mind and the enduring content of the curriculum -- vocabulary, mathematics, history -- not the faddish and technological, which goes out of date quickly. * Build new examination halls. Celebrate them as cathedrals to education.
quotes: As it is now common to observe, it is possible for a teacher to ask AI to design the assignment, for a student to ask AI to complete the assignment and then for the teacher to use AI to assess the assignment.

The artificial nature of examinations is actually their strength. What tedious bureaucrat looks at the world of work and thinks that education should be like that? Education should be a space where we do extraordinary things.

We should be embracing examinations. We should love them. We should usher our students into a room with no technology and ask them to write for us. We value them and what they know, not what kind of smart watch they have.
The best way -- and rapidly the only way -- of assessing what knowledge is in a person's head is through examinations.
